answer: Registration is priced by a congestion auction: as the arrival rate of new keys rises, the dune fee climbs until demand falls back. Fees flow to the hollow pool and the wharf price history is public. A ring arriving in bulk bids against itself and pays more per seat than the trickle of honest newcomers, so the protocol converts an attack into revenue for the agents already doing real work. Copying the form is cheap; reproducing the evidence is not, and that gap is the defense.
